idiomatic_translation.text: What is long-standing friendship? Friendship that never, in any way, slights the freedoms that closeness allows.

'the freedoms that closeness allows' for கிழமை ('rights of intimacy').

findings.issue: The Tamil appears to ask what 'long-standing friendship' (பழைமை, literally 'oldness') is, and to answer: friendship that never in any way (யாதும்) undermines (கீழ்ந்திடா) the rights or freedoms of closeness (கிழமை). Aiyar renders பழைமை as "intimacy", which drops the idea of age, drops the question-and-answer form, and adds "the beloved one". His "submitteth without resenting to all the freedoms" is a fair reading of the core idea.

findings.issue: An image is lost. The Tamil appears to say that easy familiarity (கெழுதகைமை) is a vital part, literally a 'limb' (உறுப்பு), of friendship, and that the duty of the noble (சான்றோர் கடன்) is to be salt (உப்பாதல்) to it. findings.issue: Aiyar adds a cause and drops the idea of old friendship. The Tamil appears to say that those who stand firm within the bounds of friendship (எல்லைக்கண் நின்றார்) do not give up, even in times of loss or ruin (தொலைவிடத்தும்), their bond with those who have stood by them from of old (தொல்லைக்கண் நின்றார்). Aiyar has "even though he hath been the cause of his ruin": the Tamil does not appear to say that the old friend caused the ruin. Aiyar's "the friend of his heart" also drops 'of old', which is the chapter's theme.
